paper_type: HCI model-based reinforcement-learning method with empirical and simulation evaluation
reader_conclusion: The adaptive-menu case supports the proposed conservative planning policy versus two baselines; broad claims about adaptive interfaces across tasks, users, and UI classes require additional validation.

claims.content: The method uses model-based reinforcement learning to plan sequences of interface adaptations while predictive HCI models estimate user benefits and adaptation costs.

evidence_relations.reason: The algorithmic design directly specifies planning over adaptation sequences using predictive user/interface models.

support.source_location: Method description; author project page and paper abstract
support.reason: This is a bounded description of the implemented method rather than a claim that the user model is universally accurate.

claims.content: In the adaptive-menu case, empirical and simulation results showed the proposed policy outperforming both a non-adaptive policy and a frequency-based adaptation policy.

evidence_relations.reason: The reported empirical and simulation comparisons directly support the bounded adaptive-menu performance claim.

support.source_location: Abstract; adaptive-menu empirical and simulation results
support.reason: The comparison is explicitly limited to the evaluated adaptive-menu setting and baselines.

claims.content: The approach generally improves usability for adaptive user interfaces across users, tasks, and interface classes by finding beneficial changes and avoiding harmful ones.

evidence_relations.reason: The planning formulation is general in form but depends on predictive user models.
Adaptive-menu results support one application but not arbitrary interfaces, tasks, or populations.

support.source_location: Abstract/Discussion; conservative-policy framing beyond adaptive menus
support.reason: The method's formulation is broader than the empirical evidence, which centers on adaptive menus and model assumptions; general UI effectiveness requires external validation.

reasoning_edges.added_reach: Compares the proposed planning policy with non-adaptive and frequency-based policies in the evaluated menu setting.
assumptions: The reported empirical/simulation setups are adequate to compare these policies for the studied adaptive-menu task.

reasoning_edges.added_reach: Extends one adaptive-menu empirical/simulation case to adaptive interfaces generally.
assumptions: Predictive HCI models remain accurate and the adaptation cost/benefit structure transfers across interface types and users.

usable.results: The adaptive-menu policy comparison is usable for the tested setting.
usable.methods_or_design: Planning adaptation sequences with explicit user-cost models is a reusable HCI/AI design pattern.
usable.materials_or_documentation: Open implementation and author copies improve inspectability of the method and evaluation.

downweight.worth_noticing: The conservative objective explicitly models adaptation cost, not only immediate task reward.
downweight.cautious_or_ignore: Do not treat a successful adaptive-menu case as proof of broad UI personalization effectiveness.

uncertainty_and_follow_up: Independent user studies across interface classes, tasks, user populations, and misspecified user models would test generality and robustness.
